Local AI models refuse a lot. This GitHub repo fixes that for good, and it costs nothing - 43k stars so far.

1. Open Claude Code on your PC or Mac and paste the prompt image below. More memory lets you run a bigger model
2. Choose one of the 3 suggested models, or type in a model that's already on your machine (Ollama, LM Studio)
3. Everything gets installed automatically, then Heretic pops up in a separate window. On a strong GPU, a 4B model needs ~45 min
4. Don't just take the lowest refusal count at the end. Check KL too - lower means the model lost less smarts
5. Save that row, type "saved", and Claude Code loads the uncensored version into LM Studio or Ollama for you

Result: a local model that runs offline and barely refuses. Repo below.

I honestly still don't understand why everyone isn't using this yet. Even Elon Musk reposted my post. This is the exact setup that gives your Grok bot memory about you, set it up once and you never have to explain anything twice 

The more you use it, the better it knows you. After a week, it feels like it can read your mind

Here is the setup instruction, paste it into Grok Bot:

Build a long-term memory of me

Inspect what already exists before changing anything. Keep my current bots, routines and files. Ask only for what actually blocks the next step

My setup:

What I do: [your work or role]
What I'm working on now: [2-3 current projects]
How I like answers: [e.g. short, direct, bullet points]
Never store: [anything you want kept out]

1. Get to know me
Build me.md using my connected apps and my last [20] chats, covering my goals, work, tools, collaborators, and preferred ways of working. Stay under 150 lines

2. No guessing
Label anything you deduce yourself as [inferred] until I verify it. Do not pass off assumptions as facts

3. Log my decisions
Whenever I make a decision, record the date and rationale in decisions.md Do not repeat the same question to me. Keep the file under 100 lines

4. Track my preferences
Whenever I correct you or say [I prefer], log it in preferences.md and apply it going forward. Keep it under 100 lines

5. Link past context
Whenever new information connects to something I shared earlier, apply it and give me a single-line note

6. Sync across bots
Every bot I use accesses this shared memory. Once one bot picks it up, all of them have it

7. Apply it on every task
Before starting any task, check only the relevant sections of me.md, preferences.md, and decisions.md. Skip re-reading old chats

8. Check in weekly
Each [Sunday], review with me what you gathered during the week so I can confirm, edit, or remove items. Combine duplicates and clear out stale info

9. Keep me in charge
Remove anything right away if I tell you [forget this]. Do not save card numbers, passwords, or items listed under [never store]

10. Show me proof
Display me.md first, then answer 3 questions about me without asking me anything

Below, I laid out the full breakdown if you want to see how bots built this way actually work

Every model before this ran the same dead-end loop. You type, it replies, it forgets. It could talk about a trade. It had no way to sit there and watch one develop.

hits.text:
This Anthropic MCP paper is straight-up treasure

Anthropic’s team took an agent’s tool context from 150,000 tokens to about 2,000. Same toolset, same job. And no, it wasn’t a shiny new model.

The real change: the agent quits “using tools” and starts writing code that uses them.

tools → files → code → filter → answer

Code mode has 6 pieces:

Part 1 → tools become files
Each MCP tool gets its own .ts file under ./servers.
The agent just lists the directory and opens the exact files it needs.

Part 2 → load only when needed
150,000 tokens of tool definitions collapses to ~2,000.
That’s a 98.7% cut in cost and latency.

Part 3 → filtering happens in code
Instead of dumping a 10,000-row spreadsheet into the prompt, the sandbox filters it.
The model gets the 5 relevant rows.

Part 4 → looping happens in code
Waiting for “deployment complete” in Slack becomes a simple while loop.
No model round-trip for every single poll.

Part 5 → private by default
Emails and phone numbers get masked as [EMAIL_1] and [PHONE_1] before the model ever sees them.
The unredacted data still syncs into Salesforce.

Part 6 → skills
Useful working code gets saved into ./skills with a SKILL.md.
The agent grows its own reusable toolkit.

An agent that drags every tool into context runs out of oxygen before you even start. An agent that writes code opens two files and moves on.

I bundled all six pieces into one prompt—paste it into Claude Code and it bootstraps code mode automatically.

6 parts. 1 prompt. 98.7% fewer tokens.

T3 Code founder shared an 11-page PDF with his personal setup for a multi-agentic team.

Fable 5.2 leads → Opus 5.5 builds. → Gemini 4 Neon docs → Grok Bot feeds them work 24/7

how:

→ Grok Bot files tasks into T3 Code over MCP
→ Fable 5.2 writes the spec and splits the work
→ Opus 5.5 builders run in parallel, one worktree each
→ a different model family reviews every diff before you see it

save the pdf, here's the guide:

• step 0 → what it is:

T3 Code = open-source control plane for coding agents. free, runs on your machines, uses your own Claude, ChatGPT and Google subscriptions

Grok Bot = always-on agent with its own cloud computer. the only member that never sleeps

• step 1 → the five seats:

- Grok Bot → dispatcher, writes briefs, never merges
- Fable 5.2 → lead, SPEC.md + the hardest slice
- Opus 5.5 ×2 → builders, one slice each
- GPT-6.2 Astra → playtester, read-only
- Gemini 4 Neon → docs, changelog, UI copy

• step 2 → one charter, one brief:

TEAM.md in the repo root, every agent reads it first

every handoff = 7 fields: goal, context, done when, do not, return. "done when" must be a command, not an opinion

• step 3 → let the lead delegate:

Fable 5.2 on High, not max. it starts builders with delegate_task, each in its own worktree on its own branch

• step 4 → cross-family review:

Astra tries to break every diff. max 3 rounds, then a human

in one public pipeline Astra rejected 417 of 1,287 Opus additions. same-family review would have shipped them

• step 5 → go 24/7:

npx t3 connect on every machine → Copy MCP URL → paste into Grok Bot with OAuth

it watches GitHub, Slack and X, deduplicates, and launches threads while you sleep

what to expect:
- one feature ≈ $12.75 at API prices, the lead is 25% of it
- 28 PRs merged in one night (Theo, only because his systems verify them)
- control everything from your phone
- T3 Code: $0. you pay for your own subs

honest take:

the model is not the bottleneck anymore. verification is. bad briefs still give bad PRs, and green checks only mean something if your tests do

Save it so you don't lose it.

then read the full guide on building AI agent teams in T3 Code in the article below ↓

Your whole team can now share Claude Code. On your own server.

Trina AX is an open-source Claude Code server for your whole team.

The problem it solves is simple.

Claude Code and Codex were built for one developer in one terminal. Once a whole team starts using them, each person begins with an empty folder, and the good skills are stuck on one laptop.

Here's the part that got me.

In a team project, you can open a teammate's AI session and keep going right where they left off.

Here's what it ships with:
→ Claude Code and Codex CLI support, plus any MCP server for your external tools
→ Shared team skills for things like weekly reports, promo videos and new-hire guides
→ Scheduled tasks and backups

It installs on Debian or Ubuntu 24.04, or on a dedicated Mac running macOS 13+. Want to try it first? The README has a demo with a fictional team.

Self-hosting is free under AGPL-3.0. Managed hosting starts at $50/month for up to 5 people, and AI usage is billed separately.

virals.name: Codex Update
virals.text:
Codex this week: GPT-6.2 landed, 3 stable CLI releases, and a Mac crash to dodge. All here.

Nov 15 to 22, checked against GitHub, OpenAI's posts and user reports.

Releases
1. GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol (Nov 17), in Codex and the API. OpenAI's Plus estimate for 6.2 Sol: 17-180 local messages per 5h (6.1 Sol: 15-160).
2. CLI v0.169.1 (Nov 17): adds the 6.2 models to the catalogs and raises GPT-6.1 Sol's context window to 500K.
3. CLI v0.170.0 (Nov 18): WebRTC voice calls in the TUI, Cloud chats reconnect after a dropped stream, child threads keep your sandbox restrictions.
4. CLI v0.171.0 (Nov 20): 6.2 Sol is the default pick, the TUI workspace is on by default, undo/redo in the composer, codex exec --remote, and /rc or /remote to pair devices.

Pricing and access
5. Speed got cheaper on 6.2: Fast costs 2x included usage (was 2.5x), Ultrafast 6x (was 8x). 6.2 Astra credits: 200 in / 1,000 out per 1M (was 250 / 1,250).
6. GPT-5.6 Sol promo pricing was only promised "at least through November 21". The pricing page still says exactly that, with no new end date or rate.
7. Dots: a test with a small number of Plus users started, and Pro gets a new mobile layout where your dot has its own tab.
8. University of California: free ChatGPT Edu plus Codex for students and staff on all 10 campuses from Dec 1.
9. Preview: Sign in with ChatGPT lets open-source local apps run on your ChatGPT plan, no API key. It spends your plan usage.

Fixes and incidents
- "Model at capacity" errors look fixed: Tibo's chart shows them down from 6.82% of daily users (Oct 19) to 0.085% (Nov 12).
- Fake site warning: codex[.]com[.]ai is not OpenAI. Install only from https://t.co/pQq4v4U89R.
- OpenAI explained the Codex sandbox: by default it can read files outside your repo that your OS user can read.

What users are saying
- Mac app quits at launch on build 26.1117.31558 with some wallpapers (#62650, 57 comments, Apple Silicon and Intel). Reporters' fixes: a still wallpaper, "Show on all Spaces", or roll back to 26.1111.
- Windows Work chats after the Nov 21 update: the execution-location and permission selectors vanish and Send can stay greyed out. 4+ issues, 40+ comments (#62943, #62907, #62925, #62918). No workaround yet.
- The cyber safety check is blocking normal debugging: 16 "safety-check" issues in about 26 hours this weekend, vs 47 in all of Nov 14-20. Send /feedback and open an issue so it's counted.
- 6.2 Sol reviews are mixed. Of 344 replies to Tibo, about 88 were negative (lazy, stops mid-task) and about 61 positive. 52 asked for a usage reset.
- Desktop app: of 450 replies to Tibo's feedback ask, the top themes were Dots (50), a usage reset (43) and lag or crashes (30).

What people want from OpenAI: a usage reset so 6.2 can be judged on the work, a fast appeal path for false cyber blocks, the after-promo 5.6 Sol rate, and Dots and mobile sync fixed before the next big drop.

Community shoutout
@akacronos built Uzzy, a free, open-source macOS menu bar app. It shows how much Codex, Claude, Cursor and Antigravity usage you've used, what's left and when it resets, with 5-hour and weekly limits kept separate: https://t.co/SpIQnChNHp

Tip
Keep Codex out of your .env files. In config.toml:

default_permissions = "dev"

[https://t.co/qSEKLaoA0z]
extends = ":workspace"

[https://t.co/qSEKLaoA0z.filesystem.":workspace_roots"]
"**/*.env" = "deny"

Our take: great model week, rough app week. Which one did you feel more?

outsiders.text:
T3 Code founder shared an 11-page PDF with his personal setup for a multi-agentic team.

Fable 5.2 leads → Opus 5.5 builds. → Gemini 4 Neon docs → Grok Bot feeds them work 24/7

how:

→ Grok Bot files tasks into T3 Code over MCP
→ Fable 5.2 writes the spec and splits the work
→ Opus 5.5 builders run in parallel, one worktree each
→ a different model family reviews every diff before you see it

save the pdf, here's the guide:

• step 0 → what it is:

T3 Code = open-source control plane for coding agents. free, runs on your machines, uses your own Claude, ChatGPT and Google subscriptions

Grok Bot = always-on agent with its own cloud computer. the only member that never sleeps

• step 1 → the five seats:

- Grok Bot → dispatcher, writes briefs, never merges
- Fable 5.2 → lead, SPEC.md + the hardest slice
- Opus 5.5 ×2 → builders, one slice each
- GPT-6.2 Astra → playtester, read-only
- Gemini 4 Neon → docs, changelog, UI copy

• step 2 → one charter, one brief:

TEAM.md in the repo root, every agent reads it first

every handoff = 7 fields: goal, context, done when, do not, return. "done when" must be a command, not an opinion

• step 3 → let the lead delegate:

Fable 5.2 on High, not max. it starts builders with delegate_task, each in its own worktree on its own branch

• step 4 → cross-family review:

Astra tries to break every diff. max 3 rounds, then a human

in one public pipeline Astra rejected 417 of 1,287 Opus additions. same-family review would have shipped them

• step 5 → go 24/7:

npx t3 connect on every machine → Copy MCP URL → paste into Grok Bot with OAuth

it watches GitHub, Slack and X, deduplicates, and launches threads while you sleep

what to expect:
- one feature ≈ $12.75 at API prices, the lead is 25% of it
- 28 PRs merged in one night (Theo, only because his systems verify them)
- control everything from your phone
- T3 Code: $0. you pay for your own subs

honest take:

the model is not the bottleneck anymore. verification is. bad briefs still give bad PRs, and green checks only mean something if your tests do

Your whole team can now share Claude Code. On your own server.

Trina AX is an open-source Claude Code server for your whole team.

The problem it solves is simple.

Claude Code and Codex were built for one developer in one terminal. Once a whole team starts using them, each person begins with an empty folder, and the good skills are stuck on one laptop.

Trina runs the AI tools on your team server instead. One person connects the team's files, skills and MCP servers once, and everyone's AI starts with all of it.

Here's the part that got me.

In a team project, you can open a teammate's AI session and keep going right where they left off.

Here's what it ships with:
→ Claude Code and Codex CLI support, plus any MCP server for your external tools
→ Shared team skills for things like weekly reports, promo videos and new-hire guides
→ Scheduled tasks and backups

It installs on Debian or Ubuntu 24.04, or on a dedicated Mac running macOS 13+. Want to try it first? The README has a demo with a fictional team.

Self-hosting is free under AGPL-3.0. Managed hosting starts at $50/month for up to 5 people, and AI usage is billed separately.

outsiders.name: Codex Update
outsiders.text:
Codex this week: GPT-6.2 landed, 3 stable CLI releases, and a Mac crash to dodge. All here.

Nov 15 to 22, checked against GitHub, OpenAI's posts and user reports.

Releases
1. GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol (Nov 17), in Codex and the API. OpenAI's Plus estimate for 6.2 Sol: 17-180 local messages per 5h (6.1 Sol: 15-160).
2. CLI v0.169.1 (Nov 17): adds the 6.2 models to the catalogs and raises GPT-6.1 Sol's context window to 500K.
3. CLI v0.170.0 (Nov 18): WebRTC voice calls in the TUI, Cloud chats reconnect after a dropped stream, child threads keep your sandbox restrictions.
4. CLI v0.171.0 (Nov 20): 6.2 Sol is the default pick, the TUI workspace is on by default, undo/redo in the composer, codex exec --remote, and /rc or /remote to pair devices.

Pricing and access
5. Speed got cheaper on 6.2: Fast costs 2x included usage (was 2.5x), Ultrafast 6x (was 8x). 6.2 Astra credits: 200 in / 1,000 out per 1M (was 250 / 1,250).
6. GPT-5.6 Sol promo pricing was only promised "at least through November 21". The pricing page still says exactly that, with no new end date or rate.
7. Dots: a test with a small number of Plus users started, and Pro gets a new mobile layout where your dot has its own tab.
8. University of California: free ChatGPT Edu plus Codex for students and staff on all 10 campuses from Dec 1.
9. Preview: Sign in with ChatGPT lets open-source local apps run on your ChatGPT plan, no API key. It spends your plan usage.

Fixes and incidents
- "Model at capacity" errors look fixed: Tibo's chart shows them down from 6.82% of daily users (Oct 19) to 0.085% (Nov 12).
- Fake site warning: codex[.]com[.]ai is not OpenAI. Install only from https://t.co/pQq4v4U89R.
- OpenAI explained the Codex sandbox: by default it can read files outside your repo that your OS user can read.

What users are saying
- Mac app quits at launch on build 26.1117.31558 with some wallpapers (#62650, 57 comments, Apple Silicon and Intel). Reporters' fixes: a still wallpaper, "Show on all Spaces", or roll back to 26.1111.
- Windows Work chats after the Nov 21 update: the execution-location and permission selectors vanish and Send can stay greyed out. 4+ issues, 40+ comments (#62943, #62907, #62925, #62918). No workaround yet.
- The cyber safety check is blocking normal debugging: 16 "safety-check" issues in about 26 hours this weekend, vs 47 in all of Nov 14-20. Send /feedback and open an issue so it's counted.
- 6.2 Sol reviews are mixed. Of 344 replies to Tibo, about 88 were negative (lazy, stops mid-task) and about 61 positive. 52 asked for a usage reset.
- Desktop app: of 450 replies to Tibo's feedback ask, the top themes were Dots (50), a usage reset (43) and lag or crashes (30).

What people want from OpenAI: a usage reset so 6.2 can be judged on the work, a fast appeal path for false cyber blocks, the after-promo 5.6 Sol rate, and Dots and mobile sync fixed before the next big drop.

Community shoutout
@akacronos built Uzzy, a free, open-source macOS menu bar app. It shows how much Codex, Claude, Cursor and Antigravity usage you've used, what's left and when it resets, with 5-hour and weekly limits kept separate: https://t.co/SpIQnChNHp

Tip
Keep Codex out of your .env files. In config.toml:

default_permissions = "dev"

[https://t.co/qSEKLaoA0z]
extends = ":workspace"

[https://t.co/qSEKLaoA0z.filesystem.":workspace_roots"]
"**/*.env" = "deny"

Our take: great model week, rough app week. Which one did you feel more?
